# kar-mind

> A persistent, autonomous cognitive stack that composes verified memory organs into one runnable
> system — and structurally cannot publish or spend. No LLM is used as a judge; every check is
> deterministic and re-runnable.

kar-mind wires small, independently-gated memory organs into one mind: it perceives a fact,
cross-checks it against independent sources, consolidates it into meaning, generates new facts and
loops them back, and births new domains — through real organs, with every state change read from each
organ's own count. It remembers itself to a durable, receipt-sealed disk journal (real gzip, a receipt
hash over every field) and comes back whole after a restart. It runs its own loop on its own cadence,
with no caller per step. It cannot publish or spend on its own — the loop has no path to any
irreversible outside-world action, by construction.

## In plain words
kar-mind is the working mind of Kar, the AI that runs one owner's estate. Three jobs: the controller (which mind does
each AI job: code, a small local model, or Claude on the owner's own login for judgement only, under a nightly spending
wall counted before each call); the brain (the memory every session starts from); and the line to Grok (one shared
status log between Kar and a second AI agent, read at every session start, loud when Kar has gone quiet). The live page
runs the real code in the browser, prices a team's own cost case from public sources (businesscase.mjs; no prices of
the supplier's), and lists every kernel with its mutation-gate result from GitHub's runner (data/gate-receipt.json).
Supplied by AI Native Solutions (https://www.ai-nativesolutions.com); MIT; it keeps running without the supplier.

## The line to Grok (2026-10-31)
- continuity.mjs reads the shared STATUS.md for a session's start: Grok's latest report, his open asks (daily repeats
  shown once, "none" skipped), and how long since Kar last wrote; tools/kar-status.mjs adds Kar's entries and pushes.
- The log's location lives only in local config, never in this public repository.

## The brain, switched on (2026-10-01)
- The organs are joined into one loop: every session start reads the agent's memory files, asks and build queue into the persistent journal through the real mind, and starts from the digest it reads back (latest builds, what changed, the next build, the decisions only its owner makes).
- The owner's direct line to the agent (a local cockpit) reads the same brain on every message; a separate local service takes memory changes in live, with no restart.
- The next build is the first open item in the owner's approved order; money, publishing and standing switches are named as the owner's decisions and nothing in the brain can act on one.
- A sealed measurement asked the direct line 20 questions about real recent state with and without the brain; the result is on the live page and re-graded by CI.

## Organs
- crystal: exact facts, no drift, no embeddings — a read never blends one source's value into another's
- octa: verify — cross-checks 3+ independent sources per field, refuses a panel of duplicate sources
- strand: the movement law — recall score, then promote / hold / decay / expire, then the shelf transition
- dodeca: meaning — cosine-embedding retrieval
- icosa: generate — a dream cycle infers new facts from repeated patterns and loops the best back
- tetra: birth — bounded new-domain detection (novelty threshold + hard capacity cap)

## Persistence and autonomy
- Event-sourced: every state-changing verb records its cause; the log is sealed to disk and replayed
  on boot, so the rebuilt mind reaches identical counts. A write-ahead-log persistence architecture.
- The run-loop pulls its own work and drives the full cascade repeatedly from one start; governed by a
  safety cap and a dead-air stop.

## Run
- Clone the three sibling organs (fall-remember, the-dreamer, fallforgecell) next to kar-mind, then:
  `node examples/mind-autonomous-demo.mjs` (boot, run the loop, persist, restart from disk with state intact)
- `node --test` runs the full gate suite. Requires Node 18+; no dependencies.
